key_insight: Encoder--decoder operator learning can be analyzed in a resolution-independent way by showing that the induced kernels converge to a limiting kernel, so error bounds no longer depend on the particular encoding resolution.
engineering_relevance: This gives practical guarantees for training operator-learning models at changing discretization levels, including encoder--decoder neural networks, with explicit tradeoffs between optimization, regularization, encoding error, and finite-width effects.
method: Map matrix-valued kernels on encoded data to operator-valued kernels on the original function spaces via isometric RKHS equivalence.
Prove operator-norm convergence of induced integral operators to a limiting kernel as input/output resolution increases.
Derive upper and lower error bounds for regularized SGD and extend the analysis to limiting NTKs for wide encoder--decoder networks.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical upper and lower bounds, plus polynomial parameter and sample complexity guarantees when encoding errors decay algebraically.
watch_item: The guarantees rely on asymptotic kernel convergence and finite-width corrections, so performance can still be sensitive to the chosen encoding and how quickly its approximation error decays in practice.
paper_title: Resolution-Independent Analysis of Encoder--Decoder Operator Learning via Limiting Kernels
